title: Overhead Power Lines
whatItIs: Contact with live overhead lines kills and injures people every year. Cranes, tippers, excavators, MEWPs and long items such as scaffold tubes and ladders are the usual causes.

keyFacts.text: By law, work near overhead power lines MUST be carefully planned to avoid accidental contact.

keyFacts: Always assume a line is live until its owner confirms it is dead.
Best: avoid working near the line. If you can't, ask the owner to divert it or switch it off.
Plan controls for any work within 10 m of the line, measured at ground level from below the nearest wire.
Ground-level barriers keep plant out of a safety zone 6 m either side of the nearest wire.
Lines on wooden poles can be power lines, not phone wires. Contact can kill at 230 V.

visual.caption: If plant or equipment touches an overhead line (HSE GS6)

items.title: Don't touch the wires
items.text: Assume they are live: dead lines can be switched back on.

items.title: Get help
items.text: Call the emergency services; say power lines are involved.

items.title: Stay in the vehicle
items.text: Or jump well clear. Never touch vehicle and ground together.

items.title: Keep away
items.text: Ground near a fallen wire may be live. Wait for the owner's all-clear.

a.label: Barriers (no work under the line)
points: Ground-level barriers mark a safety zone
Zone runs 6 m either side of the nearest wire
No storing materials or plant inside it

b.label: Goalposts (plant must cross)
points: A fenced passageway under the line
Lower jibs, booms and tipper bodies to cross

onTheTest.question: A tipper lorry's raised body has touched an overhead power line. The driver is unhurt. What is the safest advice?
options: Stay in the cab, or jump clear without touching cab and ground
Lower the tipper body, then walk away
Ask a workmate to pull you out of the cab
onTheTest.why: GS6 para 31: stay in the vehicle or, if you must get out, jump as far as you can. Don't touch the vehicle from the ground.

onTheTest.question: Plant must work near, but not under, an overhead line. How far from the nearest wire should the ground-level safety zone extend?
onTheTest.why: GS6 para 19: the safety zone should extend 6 m horizontally either side of the nearest wire. HSG150 para 499 agrees.

traps: You don't have to touch a line to get hurt: electricity can arc across a gap.
Insulating guards or proximity alarms on plant are not enough on their own.
Carry long items like ladders and tubes flat and close to the ground.
The contractor doing the work stays responsible for precautions, not the line owner.
